blocks.x: We might put your name on here first if you'll give your full name, your middle name and all too, if you have a middle name.
Well, are we ready? Yes, we're all ready. Well, my name is Frank Joseph Christian. And I'll leave my address. Yes, oh, it would be nice to have you. I live now at 30...
I'll make a note on here that the day is September 7th, 1965. Also that Al Rose is here helping with this interview and this is Bill Russell. So we'll have a record of the voices. You

were talking about Bill Galladay's band. Yeah, Bill used to play. You see, Bill couldn't, all the songs he used to get, he heard him a couple of times, he'd try to get him out and then play him, you see it.
George, George Burgess. He didn't play though. He didn't play.
He played clarinet. He used to play with us.
Who, George?
Yeah.
What did he play?
He played clarinet.
Clarinet, I see.
What I see, they had no pictures of him.
Uh-huh.
And Leo Grillo and Rick Roland on clarinet.
Oh yes, he was a big fella.
Yeah. Yeah, you saw him in the pictures.
Yes.

Uh-huh. Yeah, I wanted to tell you about that the other day. I thought about him. I said, Rick Roland, he... Leo Grillo, he was a... He was a man. He... I think he played with Gallagher some. He played with me, but he wouldn't play with everybody. He was kind of a funny... Funny... Funny sort of a fella. He was an old man and he... He was particular, in other words, who he played with. He was a good clarinet player. But, uh... I don't know, he...
He was a good clarinet player. So, actually, probably when you played with Baquet, it was with Papa Lane's band. Yeah.
More than like that. Lane used to get in. Yeah.
Can you tell us about Jimmy Durante? Was he a good pianist? Or how did he play?
Well, Jimmy was...
Was he a comedian then too? He was pretty good.

Jimmy was alright. Jimmy had a... Jimmy had a number for everybody who used to come in the place. Everyone. And they all knew it. They all knew he'd give them all... He used to play a piece for every one of the waiters. He used to call them one of them walking the dog. And one of them would come slim. All had a different name. And he had a... He had a tune he used to play for every one of them. And when he'd... In between songs like that he'd play... And he'd... He'd just give a chord... Or sometime he'd make them stand up and wave at him. He'd say... He'd say, now watch... Watch walking the dog. And he'd shout on the piano. He'd shout... Na na na na... Na na na na...
He'd stand up and wave. He'd play...

He'd play another song. Na na na na na na na na na na na na na na na. And she knows that over there. He said, I watch so and so. Maybe some girl would be over there. And he'd play, along come Nancy, along come Daisy. She would be here. He had a number for every one of them. Where was this? Where was this, Frank?
In New York. I mean, do you remember the name of the place? Alamo. The Alamo?
On Broadway or around, where was that?
Oh, it was on, I think it was 158, I think.
Uh-huh. Did you also play at Coney Island with him?
Yeah, I went to Coney Island, yeah.
Can you tell us about the records you made up there? Do you remember when you made those, or what company, and what the tune was?
I played that Jada. I played that Jada on an old K record, I believe. I used to have that.
I don't have it, brother. Under your own name? As Frank? No.
No, I played it in the band. In the band I played it in. I played a couple of numbers that I played, but I can't remember the things.
You don't remember who you were playing with though, huh?
No, they had a band, but I hardly knew them.
In New York? Yeah. A jazz band or a big band?

Yeah, it was a jazz band, part of a jazz band. And I played a couple of records. I was paid outright for it. I don't even know. I made some Columbia records. I don't think I made it. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.

segments.title: Opening: name, address and date of the interview
segments.summary: Russell asks for Christian's full name; he gives Frank Joseph Christian and his address, and Russell notes the date and that Al Rose is present.

segments.title: Bill Gallaty's band and how Bill learned songs by ear
segments.summary: Christian recalls bandleader Bill Galladay, who could pick up songs after hearing them a couple of times and then play them.

segments.title: Clarinetists George Baquet, Leo Grillo and Rick Roland; Papa Laine's band
segments.summary: Christian and Rose discuss clarinetists who played with him, including Baquet and the particular, respected Leo Grillo, and Rose suggests Christian played with Baquet in Papa Laine's band.

segments.title: Jimmy Durante at the Alamo and Coney Island
segments.summary: Christian describes how Durante played a special tune for each waiter and customer at the Alamo in New York, and confirms playing with him at Coney Island.

segments.title: Recording 'Ja-Da' and other records made in New York
segments.summary: Christian recalls playing on a record of Ja-Da and a few others with a jazz band he hardly knew, being paid outright, and possibly Columbia records.
